name: North Route (North Peak)
approach: Drive Silver-Skagit Road from Hope, B.C. to its southern end at Hozomeen (subject to the NPS border-gate closure - verify first). Start at the Hozomeen ranger station, elevation about 1,600 ft, and follow the little Trail of the Obelisk loop. Leave it eastward, cross Howlett Creek, and climb cross-country through moderately open forest on Hozomeen's western flank. There is no trail from here on; the forest is passable on the ascent but reports describe dense brush and jackstraw deadfall as a serious time sink on the way down. Continue to a heathery knoll at about 5,900 ft where you gain the north ridge proper. Round trip is roughly 15 miles with 6,800 ft of gain and the same in loss.

access.fees: No park entrance fee. Hozomeen Campground is free and first-come, first-served, late May through October. Backcountry permits $10 per person plus $6 reservation fee; 15 and under free.
access.permit: No permit needed for a day climb, which is how this route is usually done. Any overnight bivouac on the ridge requires an NPS wilderness permit for the relevant cross-country zone, reserved through Recreation.gov and issued by email after the safety video, or picked up in person at Marblemount.
access.closures: NPS border gate at Hozomeen closed to vehicle and foot traffic since 2020; still closed, with no end date given, on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026. Silver-Skagit Road closed to the public at the km 6 gate since 24 July 2026 for wildfire; no end date given in the B.C. Ministry of Transportation and Transit advisory last updated 8 September 2026. NPS has also closed the entire Hozomeen area and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone for the Border 2 Fire, no end date given as of that 14 September 2026 page. All three must be verified before the trip.
access.landManager: National Park Service - Ross Lake National Recreation Area, North Cascades National Park Complex. Approach drive crosses B.C. Parks' Skagit Valley Provincial Park.
access.passRequired: No US trailhead pass. Passport or NEXUS required because the drive is through Canada, with entry and re-entry at a staffed port of entry - Hozomeen is not one.

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades NP wilderness permit for the lake and cross-country camps; none for the drive-in campground
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov or get one at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center before the trip. Hozomeen Campground itself is first come, first served.

road.name: Silver-Skagit Road (Skagit Valley Road) from Hope, British Columbia
road.status: Roughly 37 miles / 60 km of gravel, graded periodically but usually washboarded and potholed; a spare tire is standard advice. Rebuilt following the 2021 B.C. flood washouts. Closed at km 6 as of 24 July 2026 for the Border 2 Fire, which crossed into B.C. from Washington 2.4 km east of Hozomeen.
road.driveNote: Hwy 1 Exit 168 at Hope, Flood-Hope Road, then Silver-Skagit Road south to its end at Hozomeen. About 1 to 1.5 hours. This route starts at the very end of the road at the ranger station, so the border-gate closure blocks it completely when in force.
road.seasonalGate: B.C. seasonal winter shutdown posted 15 October 2025 to 14 April 2026. The NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen has separately been closed to both vehicles and foot traffic since 2020, with no end date given on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026.
